title: Fortnightly Nudge Lab — Sprint Notes & Metrics
content:
Snapshot: quick two-week check-in (notes messy — intentional). Goal is to keep momentum on micro-outcomes and test one nudge per week. Focus areas: deep work blocks, demo cadence, short docs shipped.

What I measured (last 14 days):
- Deep focus sessions (>=90m): 5 (target 8) — biggest drop Tue/Thu due to meetings
- Demos shipped: 2 small walkthroughs (one recorded) — wanted 3
- Writing: 2 short notes (this + roadmap sketch) — target 4
- Context switches per day (estimate): 12–18 — target <8
- Happiness / energy (self-rated): 6/10 -> 7/10 by weekend

Signals I care about (fast proxies):
- # of uninterrupted blocks (>=60m)
- number of artifacts pushed (PRs, notes, demos)
- ratio: outcome/article per focused block (goal 0.5)

Hypotheses to test next cycle:
H1: If I reserve first 2 hours as immutable "deep" (no async), then interrupted blocks drop and PR output + demo readiness increase.
H2: A single morning slack nudge (automated message to myself) that states the priority for the day increases probability of completing the top 1 by EOD from 40% -> 70%.
H3: Reducing meeting length to 25m with explicit agenda decreases context switches by ~30%.

Nudge experiments (run in parallel):
- Week 1 nudge: calendar-only window (05:30–07:30) + auto-status 'do-not-disturb' for Slack; measure deep sessions. TODO: add calendar block template.
- Week 2 nudge: morning micro-brief (one-line goal pinned in Slack DM with myself + Aria) at 09:05; measure completed top-1.
- Bonus micro-experiment: attach a 10-min post-block note habit to solidify learning (tiny friction).

Concrete actions (next 14 days):
- Create calendar template and share with Aria; put calendar block on recurring days M/W/F (Riley) — due 2026-03-12
- Build a 1-min demo checklist for recording (title, 3 bullets, 30s highlight) — due 2026-03-14
- Convert two long meetings to two 25m slots + async prep doc (try for two recurring meetings) — ask Devon to pilot — due 2026-03-16
- Capture three short write-ups from demos and link to Confluence personal space (goal: 4/14 days)

Retro: what went well
- Momentum spikes after mid-week deep session; felt tangible progress on one small infra task.
- Recording one demo forced crispness -> immediate helpful feedback.

Retro: friction / blockers
- Meetings slipped into deep blocks twice (back-to-back scheduling leak).
- Habit friction: I skip the post-block note when hungry/tired — need <3-min pattern.
- Over-commit: said yes to two syncs that were low-signal; should triage with 'agenda required' rule.

Decisions & rules to adopt now
- Immutable deep windows MWF 09:00–11:00 (start small: protect 2h)
- Meeting rule: any recurring meeting needs a stated outcome and <25m preferred; else decline or convert to async recap
- Nudge rule: one pinned morning priority only (max 1)

Open questions / friction to resolve
- Can calendar auto-accept only essential invites during deep window? (Ask SRE or GA admin)
- Is there a lightweight tool to DM yourself pinned notes each morning? (Zapier/Slack automation?)

Quick wins (2–7 days):
- Put all non-essential meetings to 'optional' and try one week with protected deep windows
- Record 1x 3-min demo and post to personal notes + ask for one piece of feedback

Notes to self / voice memo prompts:
- "What was the 60-minute win today?" (answer in notes)
- "If I only shipped one thing this week, would it move the needle?"

Loose thoughts / fragments:
- Possibility: create a tiny 'nudge' script that posts morning priority to a private channel and pings at 2pm if not marked done. Could be GitHub action -> Slack.
- Consider pairing with Devon for one deep session/week to mirror accountability (30m break halfway).

End-of-doc check: capture these into Confluence + tag demo notes with #nudge-lab. Keep this as a rolling fortnightly log.

Quick links / references:
- Personal nudge space (Confluence): https://confluence.internal.redwood/personal-nudge-lab
- Related ticket: JIRA-4281 (calendar-template)

- 2026-03-10: refined actions, added meeting-length experiment (Devon)
